world.title: France to deploy 70,000 officers as Halloween protests raise disorder fears
world.summary: France will deploy about 70,000 police officers and gendarmes on Saturday, Oct. 31, as Yellow Vest activists and student unions call for another day of nationwide protests and Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez warns of a “very high” risk of disorder. Authorities plan to restrict demonstrations in city centres, increase p
world.content: France will deploy about 70,000 police officers and gendarmes on Saturday, Oct. 31, as Yellow Vest activists and student unions call for another day of nationwide protests and Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez warns of a “very high” risk of disorder. Authorities plan to restrict demonstrations in city centres, increase protection for shops and ban gatherings they say were promoted online as Halloween events; approved demonstrations will still be allowed. Protesters are demonstrating against rising living costs and inequality, while student demonstrations over school conditions have drawn broader demands on wages and public services. Nationwide demonstrations on Oct. 17 escalated into riots, looting and vandalism, and authorities acknowledged security and intelligence failures. Rallies on Oct. 24 were largely peaceful, though some street violence occurred. The Interior Ministry said 410,000 people marched on Oct. 24, while unions estimated about twice that number. The government announced measures on Oct. 26, including replacing the university admissions platform and offering loans for school renovations, but student representatives said their concerns about police conduct remained unresolved. Unions and students have also called a nationwide strike for Nov. 5, while the government says security forces will act firmly against violence this weekend.
world.image_alt: France to deploy 70,000 officers as Halloween protests raise disorder fears

world.title: Italian EU peacekeeping helicopter crash in Bosnia kills four, injures 11
world.summary: An Italian CH-47 Chinook helicopter with the European Union peacekeeping force (EUFOR) in Bosnia and Herzegovina crashed during routine training near Gorice, in the Brčko district, on Thursday, Oct. 29, killing four people and injuring 11. The dead were two Italian soldiers and two members of the Italian Red Cross Volu
world.content: An Italian CH-47 Chinook helicopter with the European Union peacekeeping force (EUFOR) in Bosnia and Herzegovina crashed during routine training near Gorice, in the Brčko district, on Thursday, Oct. 29, killing four people and injuring 11. The dead were two Italian soldiers and two members of the Italian Red Cross Volunteer Military Corps; the 11 injured were receiving treatment and were reported to be in stable condition. The helicopter carried 15 people. No civilians were injured, and no civilian infrastructure, property or vehicles were damaged, EUFOR said. The aircraft was part of Operation Althea, the EU mission that oversees the military provisions of the Dayton Peace Agreement. EUFOR and Italy’s Defence Ministry said investigations were underway to establish the cause, and the force said it would release further information after verification.
world.image_alt: Italian EU peacekeeping helicopter crash in Bosnia kills four, injures 11

world.title: Russia and Ukraine dispatch aid convoy as Oleshky evacuation window opens
world.summary: Russia and Ukraine sent a humanitarian convoy toward Russian-occupied Oleshky on Friday as an evacuation window opened under a local ceasefire brokered by U.S. first lady Melania Trump. The convoy began moving overnight with food and medical supplies after officials said they had cleared mines from its routes. The six-
world.content: Russia and Ukraine sent a humanitarian convoy toward Russian-occupied Oleshky on Friday as an evacuation window opened under a local ceasefire brokered by U.S. first lady Melania Trump. The convoy began moving overnight with food and medical supplies after officials said they had cleared mines from its routes. The six-day truce began Oct. 27 and covers the frontline town, where about 2,000 residents have faced months of food, water and medicine shortages. Residents who wanted to leave had until 2 p.m. local time Friday; aid distribution for those staying was scheduled to start after 2:30 p.m. at the town’s central district hospital. Russian human rights commissioner Yana Lantratova said two people, including a sapper, died during the mine clearance operation. The evacuation fleet includes 25 buses with at least 750 seats, according to Lantratova. The ceasefire is scheduled to last through late Nov. 1. The pause is limited to Oleshky and its surrounding area. Russian attacks elsewhere in Ukraine continued, including a drone strike on a Dnipro railway station that killed at least 14 people.
world.image_alt: Russia and Ukraine dispatch aid convoy as Oleshky evacuation window opens

world.title: Australian appeals court sentences Erin Patterson to life without parole
world.summary: Victoria’s Court of Appeal on Friday rejected Erin Patterson’s challenge to her convictions for murdering three relatives with a meal laced with death-cap mushrooms and resentenced her to life in prison without parole. The three-judge panel also granted prosecutors’ appeal against her original sentence, which had allow
world.content: Victoria’s Court of Appeal on Friday rejected Erin Patterson’s challenge to her convictions for murdering three relatives with a meal laced with death-cap mushrooms and resentenced her to life in prison without parole. The three-judge panel also granted prosecutors’ appeal against her original sentence, which had allowed her to seek parole after 33 years. The court said Patterson carefully planned the crimes and maintained her intent to kill all four lunch guests for nearly three weeks. Her estranged husband’s parents, Don and Gail Patterson, and Gail’s sister, Heather Wilkinson, died after the July 2023 lunch at Patterson’s Leongatha home. Heather’s husband, Ian Wilkinson, survived, and Patterson was convicted of his attempted murder. The judges dismissed all seven grounds of Patterson’s appeal, including claims that trial irregularities deprived her of a fair hearing. She can still seek special leave to appeal to Australia’s High Court; the BBC reported she has 28 days to decide whether to apply.
world.image_alt: Australian appeals court sentences Erin Patterson to life without parole

world.title: China expels 33 senior officials as Xi tightens party discipline
world.summary: China’s ruling Communist Party expelled 33 senior officials at the close of a four-day leadership meeting in Beijing on Oct. 29, confirming the removal of former senior military commander Zhang Youxia, former Xinjiang party chief Ma Xingrui and others. Sixteen of those expelled were from the military. The party’s commu
world.content: China’s ruling Communist Party expelled 33 senior officials at the close of a four-day leadership meeting in Beijing on Oct. 29, confirming the removal of former senior military commander Zhang Youxia, former Xinjiang party chief Ma Xingrui and others. Sixteen of those expelled were from the military. The party’s communiqué cited serious disciplinary and legal violations without detailing individual allegations. Only 279 of the 376 full and alternate Central Committee members appointed in 2022 attended — the lowest attendance at a plenum under President Xi Jinping, with a record number of empty seats. Purges have reduced the seven-member Central Military Commission, which commands China’s armed forces, to Xi and General Zhang Shengmin, a military anti-corruption official. The party promoted Zhang Shengmin to the Politburo at the meeting. The meeting focused on internal discipline and anti-corruption, while analysts differ on whether the drive chiefly addresses graft or reinforces Xi’s authority. The party also confirmed that its 21st congress will take place in Beijing in the second half of 2027, when it will reshuffle its leadership and Xi is widely expected to seek a fourth term.
world.image_alt: China expels 33 senior officials as Xi tightens party discipline

world.title: Venezuelan opposition leader returns, presses for 2027 presidential vote
world.summary: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado returned to Caracas after nearly 10 months in exile and said Thursday that presidential elections should be held in 2027, citing a transition plan outlined by U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio. She said her own team, not a government, arranged her return and thanked P
world.content: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado returned to Caracas after nearly 10 months in exile and said Thursday that presidential elections should be held in 2027, citing a transition plan outlined by U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio. She said her own team, not a government, arranged her return and thanked President Donald Trump’s administration for capturing former President Nicolás Maduro in January. Interim President Delcy Rodríguez also said elections would be held but set no date. She said they would follow reforms and be organized by a renewed electoral authority. Machado said she had received no message from Rodríguez and is not part of Washington-backed talks between the government and opposition factions, though she wants the talks to succeed. Machado’s party is excluded from the talks, which are addressing changes to the Supreme Court and electoral council. U.S. officials have said Rodríguez should leave office in 2027 after those reforms. Machado also criticized a U.S.-Venezuela oil agreement for lacking transparency.
world.image_alt: Venezuelan opposition leader returns, presses for 2027 presidential vote

world.title: Lagarde to leave ECB early, opening succession race before French election
world.summary: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde will leave her post on Feb. 7, 2027, about nine months before her eight-year term expires. She said she wants to speak on issues beyond monetary policy and cannot comfortably maintain the neutrality her role requires. She announced the decision on Oct. 29, after the ban
world.content: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde will leave her post on Feb. 7, 2027, about nine months before her eight-year term expires. She said she wants to speak on issues beyond monetary policy and cannot comfortably maintain the neutrality her role requires. She announced the decision on Oct. 29, after the bank held its key deposit rate at 2.5%. Her departure opens a contest among European Union leaders to fill the presidency before France’s presidential election, expected in April or May 2027. Former Dutch central bank chief Klaas Knot and former Spanish central bank governor Pablo Hernández de Cos are among the leading contenders. Leaders may negotiate the succession alongside two other appointments: executive board member Isabel Schnabel is due to leave in January, and chief economist Philip Lane’s term ends in May. Eurozone inflation reached 3.8% in September, above the ECB’s 2% target, while rising energy costs and government bond yields are tightening borrowing conditions. The bank said it would continue setting policy meeting by meeting; its next Governing Council meeting is scheduled for Dec. 17.
world.image_alt: Lagarde to leave ECB early, opening succession race before French election

world.title: Pentagon fires senior Army planner as leak inquiry reaches Justice Department
world.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth removed Army Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia from his post overseeing strategy, plans and policy for the Joint Chiefs of Staff on Wednesday. According to an internal investigation report described by Axios, Sylvia acknowledged on video that he had shared classified information about the wars in Ira
world.content: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth removed Army Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia from his post overseeing strategy, plans and policy for the Joint Chiefs of Staff on Wednesday. According to an internal investigation report described by Axios, Sylvia acknowledged on video that he had shared classified information about the wars in Iran and Ukraine with journalists over roughly a year. A Pentagon official said Sylvia was accused of disclosing classified information and had failed three polygraph tests; the report Axios reviewed says he failed four. Two other Pentagon sources told CBS News the accusations were not true. A colleague told The Washington Post that Sylvia had denied leaking classified material but acknowledged contact with reporters. Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said the case had been referred to the Justice Department for possible legal action. The Justice Department said it was investigating possible leaks of classified information. The Pentagon said U.S. Central Command, not Sylvia’s Joint Staff directorate, is responsible for operational planning for the Iran war. No replacement for Sylvia has been announced.
world.image_alt: Pentagon fires senior Army planner as leak inquiry reaches Justice Department

business.title: U.S. officials suspected Megaspeed executive with ties to Nvidia chief was a Chinese intelligence asset
business.summary: U.S. intelligence agencies concluded that Alice Huang, a senior executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed, was a Chinese intelligence asset who passed information to Beijing, and suspected she had developed a close relationship with Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang, The New York Times reported. The
business.content: U.S. intelligence agencies concluded that Alice Huang, a senior executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed, was a Chinese intelligence asset who passed information to Beijing, and suspected she had developed a close relationship with Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang, The New York Times reported. The investigation began with suspicions that Megaspeed helped Chinese firms obtain restricted Nvidia AI chips. Officials reportedly worried that Alice Huang could learn about Nvidia’s plans and Jensen Huang’s efforts to influence U.S. chip policy. Nvidia said Jensen Huang’s contact with Alice Huang was routine customer engagement and that Megaspeed received no sensitive trade secrets or national-security information. The company also said allegations that Megaspeed diverted chips had been investigated and debunked. The Times reported that President Donald Trump was briefed on the intelligence findings about a year ago, but Jensen Huang received no defensive briefing. Officials reportedly feared that warning him could compromise ongoing surveillance.
business.image_alt: U.S. officials suspected Megaspeed executive with ties to Nvidia chief was a Chinese intelligence asset

business.title: Polymarket pledges refunds after breach drains international traders’ accounts
business.summary: Polymarket halted its international prediction-market exchange for about an hour on Oct. 29 after a security breach involving a third-party provider led to unauthorized withdrawals from users’ accounts. Trading resumed that afternoon, and the company pledged to reimburse affected customers. Analytics firms estimated wi
business.content: Polymarket halted its international prediction-market exchange for about an hour on Oct. 29 after a security breach involving a third-party provider led to unauthorized withdrawals from users’ accounts. Trading resumed that afternoon, and the company pledged to reimburse affected customers. Analytics firms estimated withdrawals of about $2.7 million across roughly 710 wallets, but Polymarket has not confirmed the total loss or the number of affected traders. A person familiar with the incident identified the provider as DebugBear, a UK-based website performance-monitoring company. Cybersecurity researchers said a script served through the provider searched for active trading sessions and attempted to move users’ assets. The incident affected Polymarket’s international platform, not its separate U.S. exchange. Polymarket told users that reimbursements below $10,000 were due by Oct. 30, while larger claims required a signed release.
business.image_alt: Polymarket pledges refunds after breach drains international traders’ accounts

business.title: Michigan city tops U.S. News 2027 retirement ranking for second year
business.summary: Midland, Michigan, ranked as the best U.S. city for retirement in U.S. News & World Report’s 2027 list, taking the top spot for a second consecutive year. The ranking assessed more than 850 cities on quality of life, affordability, health care, retiree taxes, job-market conditions, and population and migration patterns
business.content: Midland, Michigan, ranked as the best U.S. city for retirement in U.S. News & World Report’s 2027 list, taking the top spot for a second consecutive year. The ranking assessed more than 850 cities on quality of life, affordability, health care, retiree taxes, job-market conditions, and population and migration patterns among people 55 and older. U.S. News gave affordability more weight in its scoring, citing its importance to retirees. Six Texas cities and two Florida cities made the top 15; Homosassa Springs, Florida, ranked second and Weirton, West Virginia, third. Midland’s cost of living, quality of life and retiree tax advantages helped it retain the top spot.
business.image_alt: Michigan city tops U.S. News 2027 retirement ranking for second year

business.title: Intel warns of PC slump and supply constraints, shares fall 23%
business.summary: Intel shares fell about 23% in after-hours trading Thursday after the chipmaker forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, below analysts’ estimate of roughly $17.1 billion. It projected adjusted earnings of 25 cents a share, compared with expectations of 43 cents. Intel cited falling PC demand as h
business.content: Intel shares fell about 23% in after-hours trading Thursday after the chipmaker forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, below analysts’ estimate of roughly $17.1 billion. It projected adjusted earnings of 25 cents a share, compared with expectations of 43 cents. Intel cited falling PC demand as higher memory prices raise device costs, manufacturing constraints that have prevented it from meeting demand for data-center chips, and an explosion at its Kiryat Gat plant in Israel. Intel said the explosion is expected to cut revenue by about $600 million across two quarters; two people died and a third was seriously injured. Intel reported third-quarter revenue of $16.51 billion, up 21% year over year, and adjusted earnings of 52 cents a share, above analysts’ estimates. Data-center and AI revenue grew 78% to $7.3 billion, while revenue in the client-computing and physical-AI group fell 5% to $8.1 billion. Finance chief David Zinsner said the PC slowdown could last through at least the first half of 2027. Intel expects no positive cash flow this year as it invests $20 billion in capacity, with spending set to rise in 2027. It is working to restart production at Kiryat Gat after a two-week shutdown.
business.image_alt: Intel warns of PC slump and supply constraints, shares fall 23%

business.title: Bank of Japan says 2% inflation target met, holds rates at 1.25%
business.summary: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) said underlying inflation was “generally consistent” with its 2% target, its first such assessment since adopting the goal in 2013. The central bank kept its short-term policy rate at 1.25% in an 8-1 vote on Friday, saying it wanted to assess the effects of September’s rate increase. Board membe
business.content: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) said underlying inflation was “generally consistent” with its 2% target, its first such assessment since adopting the goal in 2013. The central bank kept its short-term policy rate at 1.25% in an 8-1 vote on Friday, saying it wanted to assess the effects of September’s rate increase. Board member Hajime Takata dissented, seeking an increase to 1.5%. The bank raised its forecast for core inflation in fiscal 2027 to 2.6% from 2.4% and warned that inflation could exceed its target. It cited companies’ growing willingness to raise wages and prices, along with energy costs and yen depreciation, as upside risks. Governor Kazuo Ueda said the bank would assess the need for a rate increase at each meeting. Markets increasingly expect the next increase at the Dec. 17-18 meeting.
business.image_alt: Bank of Japan says 2% inflation target met, holds rates at 1.25%

business.title: Volkswagen posts €5.8 billion loss as China sales slump
business.summary: Volkswagen Group, Germany’s largest automaker, posted a €5.8 billion net loss for July through September, compared with a €1.07 billion loss a year earlier. A €6.4 billion write-down on its stake in luxury-car maker Porsche accounted for most of the exceptional charges, while weak demand in China, U.S. tariffs and lowe
business.content: Volkswagen Group, Germany’s largest automaker, posted a €5.8 billion net loss for July through September, compared with a €1.07 billion loss a year earlier. A €6.4 billion write-down on its stake in luxury-car maker Porsche accounted for most of the exceptional charges, while weak demand in China, U.S. tariffs and lower electric-vehicle profits also weighed on results. Revenue fell 6.3% to €75.3 billion. Vehicle deliveries fell 14.3% to 1.89 million. In China, deliveries dropped 38.5% to about 405,800 as local manufacturers intensified competition in the world’s largest car market. Volkswagen also recorded €1 billion in write-downs tied to its Chinese operations. The company is pursuing a €31 billion cost-saving program that could eliminate up to 100,000 jobs and put four German plants at risk of closure. Chief Financial Officer Arno Antlitz said the results required swift action; labor negotiations are due to start in November.
business.image_alt: Volkswagen posts €5.8 billion loss as China sales slump

business.title: US growth accelerates to 3.4% as investment in artificial intelligence surges
business.summary: The US economy grew at a 3.4% annualized rate in the third quarter, accelerating from 2.2% in the second quarter and exceeding economists’ forecasts, according to the Commerce Department’s advance estimate released Oct. 29. Consumer spending rose 3.8%, while private investment jumped 19.4%, driven in part by companies’
business.content: The US economy grew at a 3.4% annualized rate in the third quarter, accelerating from 2.2% in the second quarter and exceeding economists’ forecasts, according to the Commerce Department’s advance estimate released Oct. 29. Consumer spending rose 3.8%, while private investment jumped 19.4%, driven in part by companies’ purchases of equipment for artificial intelligence (AI) projects. Rising imports, including technology equipment, and falling exports weighed on growth. The Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation measure, the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index, rose 0.5% in September and 3.6% from a year earlier; core inflation was 3.1%. Higher energy costs contributed to the price increase, while consumer confidence and assessments of affordability remained weak. The Federal Reserve held its benchmark rate at 3.75% to 4% on Oct. 28, saying inflation remained elevated and it needed to assess incoming data. Economists see a possible rate increase in December. The Bureau of Economic Analysis is scheduled to publish its second estimate of third-quarter growth on Nov. 25.
business.image_alt: US growth accelerates to 3.4% as investment in artificial intelligence surges

business.title: Lagarde exit opens ECB succession as French borrowing costs rise
business.summary: European Central Bank policymakers held the deposit rate at 2.5% on Oct. 29, but President Christine Lagarde said they had seriously discussed a rate increase as energy prices and bond yields tightened financing conditions for households and businesses. Eurozone inflation reached 3.8% in September, and average 10-year
business.content: European Central Bank policymakers held the deposit rate at 2.5% on Oct. 29, but President Christine Lagarde said they had seriously discussed a rate increase as energy prices and bond yields tightened financing conditions for households and businesses. Eurozone inflation reached 3.8% in September, and average 10-year government bond yields had risen about 35 basis points since the ECB’s September forecast. France’s 10-year borrowing cost topped 5% last week for the first time since 2002. The same day, Lagarde said she would leave the Frankfurt-based central bank on Feb. 7, 2027, before the end of her eight-year term, saying she wanted to speak on issues beyond monetary policy. Her departure opens a contest to lead the institution that sets interest rates across the euro area. Markets showed little reaction to the announcement, with analysts saying the ECB’s established practices were likely to outlast its president. Investors were pricing in three further rate increases by the end of 2027, which would bring the deposit rate to 3.25%. The ECB’s next policy meeting is scheduled for Dec. 17.
business.image_alt: Lagarde exit opens ECB succession as French borrowing costs rise

science.title: OpenAI and Anthropic challenge hypothesis underpinning decades of computer science
science.summary: OpenAI and Anthropic say AI-generated proofs disprove the exponential time hypothesis, a 27-year-old assumption underlying research in theoretical computer science. The hypothesis says the work needed to solve certain problems grows exponentially as the problems become larger. If the companies’ claim holds, researchers
science.content: OpenAI and Anthropic say AI-generated proofs disprove the exponential time hypothesis, a 27-year-old assumption underlying research in theoretical computer science. The hypothesis says the work needed to solve certain problems grows exponentially as the problems become larger. If the companies’ claim holds, researchers may need to revisit research and algorithms built on that premise. Researchers have not independently verified the proofs or had time to assess them fully. OpenAI published its paper on GitHub in natural language and machine-checkable Lean format and asked researchers to examine the result. Computer scientists have begun reassessing their work, though the claim’s validity and implications remain unestablished.
science.image_alt: OpenAI and Anthropic challenge hypothesis underpinning decades of computer science

science.title: Studies find amoeba reproducing at 63°C and archaea surviving Enceladus-like chemistry
science.summary: A team identified Incendiamoeba cascadensis, a single-celled organism able to reproduce at 63°C, the highest temperature recorded for eukaryotic life. Researchers found it in geothermal springs in California’s Lassen Volcanic National Park and reported the findings in a study published in September 2026. In a separate
science.content: A team identified Incendiamoeba cascadensis, a single-celled organism able to reproduce at 63°C, the highest temperature recorded for eukaryotic life. Researchers found it in geothermal springs in California’s Lassen Volcanic National Park and reported the findings in a study published in September 2026. In a separate laboratory study, the archaeon Methanothermococcus okinawensis survived, reproduced and produced methane in liquid formulated to mimic Enceladus’s alkaline, carbon-dioxide-poor ocean. It produced methane at pH levels up to 11. The researchers say the findings show that Earth-like life could tolerate some of the moon’s conditions, not that life exists there.
science.image_alt: Studies find amoeba reproducing at 63°C and archaea surviving Enceladus-like chemistry

science.title: GPS study finds seabirds veer off course after rapid time-zone shifts
science.summary: Manx shearwaters can veer off course after rapid east-west flights shift their internal clocks out of sync with the sun, researchers reported in a study published in Science on Oct. 29. The team analyzed two decades of GPS records from 1,045 breeding birds, including 1,837 continuous flights back to their nests; naviga
science.content: Manx shearwaters can veer off course after rapid east-west flights shift their internal clocks out of sync with the sun, researchers reported in a study published in Science on Oct. 29. The team analyzed two decades of GPS records from 1,045 breeding birds, including 1,837 continuous flights back to their nests; navigational errors reached 15 degrees but added only a few kilometers to their journeys. The findings suggest the birds continue to rely on their sun compass even when familiar coastlines are visible, rather than switching entirely to visual landmarks. Researchers say the measured errors do not prevent experienced birds from getting home, but whether similar clock shifts affect young, inexperienced birds or longer migrations remains unclear.
science.image_alt: GPS study finds seabirds veer off course after rapid time-zone shifts

science.title: UN finds 252 million hectares under restoration, far short of 2030 goal
science.summary: A United Nations assessment published Oct. 29 found restoration work underway across about 252 million hectares of degraded ecosystems in 149 countries, the largest documented effort to date. That area represents about 34% of the benchmark for the global goal of placing at least 30% of degraded ecosystems under effecti
science.content: A United Nations assessment published Oct. 29 found restoration work underway across about 252 million hectares of degraded ecosystems in 149 countries, the largest documented effort to date. That area represents about 34% of the benchmark for the global goal of placing at least 30% of degraded ecosystems under effective restoration by 2030. The report says the world is not on track. Restoration is concentrated on land, where work covers 232 million hectares, compared with 11 million hectares of inland waters and 5.7 million hectares of marine and coastal ecosystems, which are degrading rapidly. The report says annual investment must rise from $64 billion to $296 billion by 2030 and calls for better implementation, financing and monitoring. It was released during the COP17 biodiversity summit in Armenia, where countries were meeting to address biodiversity commitments.
science.image_alt: UN finds 252 million hectares under restoration, far short of 2030 goal

science.title: Forecasters warn powerful El Niño could intensify floods, droughts worldwide
science.summary: Forecasters say a powerful El Niño is likely to shape weather this winter, with U.S. projections calling for warmer-than-average conditions across much of the country and above-average precipitation in several regions. Scientists expect drought in parts of southern Africa and Indonesia, and heavy rain in the Horn of Af
science.content: Forecasters say a powerful El Niño is likely to shape weather this winter, with U.S. projections calling for warmer-than-average conditions across much of the country and above-average precipitation in several regions. Scientists expect drought in parts of southern Africa and Indonesia, and heavy rain in the Horn of Africa, Peru and other regions. Swiss newspaper Der Bund reported that eastern Pacific waters are 3.5 degrees above normal and that natural climate records suggest this could be the strongest El Niño in 1,000 years. Scientists say the timing and location of its impacts remain difficult to predict. On the U.S. West Coast, El Niño-related warm-water pulses, high tides and sea-level rise are increasing coastal flood risks. Bay Area risk maps identify low-lying shorelines and airport areas, and a report warns that San Francisco International Airport could flood. December tides could be 1 to 2 feet higher than this week’s. Forecasters expect the event to peak in November and December, with coastal flooding risks continuing into January.
science.image_alt: Forecasters warn powerful El Niño could intensify floods, droughts worldwide

science.title: Hubble and Webb expose hidden structures in Carina star-forming cloud
science.summary: NASA’s Hubble and James Webb space telescopes have captured complementary views of the Cat’s Head Nebula, a star-forming pillar in the Carina Nebula about 7,500 light-years from Earth. Hubble’s visible-light image shows a dark dust column edged by glowing gas, while Webb’s infrared observations reveal details within th
science.content: NASA’s Hubble and James Webb space telescopes have captured complementary views of the Cat’s Head Nebula, a star-forming pillar in the Carina Nebula about 7,500 light-years from Earth. Hubble’s visible-light image shows a dark dust column edged by glowing gas, while Webb’s infrared observations reveal details within the dust, including stars and fine strands. The images, released Oct. 29, help astronomers examine how young stars form in gas and dust exposed to radiation from massive nearby stars. Ultraviolet radiation and stellar winds likely shaped the pillar’s outline by eroding its surroundings, while denser material resisted erosion. Webb also imaged the lower-metallicity N159 star-forming region in the Large Magellanic Cloud, while Chandra and Webb observations show young stars forming in a separate Carina cloud.
science.image_alt: Hubble and Webb expose hidden structures in Carina star-forming cloud

science.title: ISS astronauts install seventh upgraded solar array during 100th US spacewalk
science.summary: NASA astronaut Anil Menon and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk installed and unfurled the International Space Station’s seventh upgraded roll-out solar array on Oct. 29, completing a 7-hour, 11-minute spacewalk that marked the 100th U.S. spacewalk from the station. The new panel adds about 8 kilowatts of p
science.content: NASA astronaut Anil Menon and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk installed and unfurled the International Space Station’s seventh upgraded roll-out solar array on Oct. 29, completing a 7-hour, 11-minute spacewalk that marked the 100th U.S. spacewalk from the station. The new panel adds about 8 kilowatts of power to support station operations as the original arrays lose output after exceeding their 15-year design life. The crew used the Canadarm2 robotic arm to move the array to its mounting point and connected it to power channel 2A. The new arrays supplement, rather than replace, the station’s original solar wings; together, they are expected to raise available power to about 215 kilowatts. The extra capacity will support research, life-support systems and visiting spacecraft through the station’s planned 2030 retirement and controlled deorbit. The crew also completed preparatory work for the eighth and final array. Menon and Kutryk are scheduled to install it on Nov. 5, completing the five-year upgrade.
science.image_alt: ISS astronauts install seventh upgraded solar array during 100th US spacewalk

science.title: Scientists map 607,000 vertebrate cells and a fly’s entire central nervous system
science.summary: Researchers have published two large-scale maps of nervous systems: a complete brain-and-nerve-cord wiring diagram for a fly, covering about 160,000 neurons and more than 200 million connections, and a body-wide cell atlas of the adult fish Danionella cerebrum, containing 607,370 cells. The fly map links neural circuit
science.content: Researchers have published two large-scale maps of nervous systems: a complete brain-and-nerve-cord wiring diagram for a fly, covering about 160,000 neurons and more than 200 million connections, and a body-wide cell atlas of the adult fish Danionella cerebrum, containing 607,370 cells. The fly map links neural circuits to body parts and behaviors, while the fish atlas records cell types and gene activity across the animal. The fish’s roughly 12-millimeter size made whole-body profiling possible. Researchers also used the atlas to track molecular changes during brain-tissue regeneration. The fly study found that many control circuits are organized as local sensory-motor loops rather than around a single central controller.
science.image_alt: Scientists map 607,000 vertebrate cells and a fly’s entire central nervous system

sports.title: Inter and AC Milan unveil €1.2bn shared stadium to replace San Siro
sports.summary: Inter and AC Milan have unveiled plans for Generali Stadium, a 71,500-seat shared home to replace San Siro from the 2031-32 season. sports.content: Inter and AC Milan have unveiled plans for Generali Stadium, a 71,500-seat shared home to replace San Siro from the 2031-32 season. The clubs expect construction to begin in 2028 on land beside the existing ground, which they will continue to use during construction. They say the new venue is intended to improve the matchday experience and help them compete financially. The project is estimated to cost €1.2 billion. Designed by Foster + Partners and MANICA, the stadium will have a two-tier, 360-degree bowl, with steep stands behind each goal intended to bring supporters closer to the pitch and intensify crowd noise. Generali, an Italian insurance company, has secured the naming rights. Some Inter supporters protested at the unveiling against the loss of San Siro, which opened in 1926 and is slated for major demolition once the new stadium nears completion.

sports.content: Belgian rider Thibau Nys will begin his cyclocross campaign at Sunday’s Koppenbergcross in Oudenaarde, targeting a third win after victories in 2023 and 2025. Lucinda Brand, who won the race last year and three of her first five races this season, also returns to the challenging course. Nys is returning after knee surgery in March limited his road season to 30 race days without a win. He says his short preparation makes this edition especially difficult. Fem van Empel is returning on a reduced schedule, while Wout van Aert plans to race some cyclocross and Mathieu van der Poel’s participation remains uncertain.

sports.content: England beat Sri Lanka by 55 runs in Lahore on Thursday, ending their Pakistan one-day international tri-series campaign with a win after three straight defeats had ruled them out of the final. England batter Ben Duckett made a career-best 167 from 132 balls as England scored 386-5; Liam Dawson then took 4-49 to help dismiss Sri Lanka for 331 in 45.1 overs. Pavan Rathnayake made 118, but Sri Lanka lost their last five wickets for 16 runs. Captain Harry Brook's side will next tour Australia, where England are scheduled to play three ODIs and five T20 internationals in November. The tour begins with a 50-over warm-up against Western Australia XI on November 7, followed by the first ODI in Perth on November 13.

sports.title: Everton beat Newcastle 3-1 to reach Carabao Cup quarter-finals
sports.summary: Everton beat Newcastle United 3-1 at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Thursday to reach the Carabao Cup quarter-finals, where they will visit League Two side Fleetwood Town in the week beginning December 14. James Garner, midfielder Hayden Hackney and Thierno Barry scored for Everton; Dan Burn headed Newcastle’s late consolat
sports.content: Everton beat Newcastle United 3-1 at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Thursday to reach the Carabao Cup quarter-finals, where they will visit League Two side Fleetwood Town in the week beginning December 14. James Garner, midfielder Hayden Hackney and Thierno Barry scored for Everton; Dan Burn headed Newcastle’s late consolation. Everton took control with two goals before half-time, and Barry’s 69th-minute finish sealed the win. Goalkeeper Jordan Pickford made several saves as Newcastle pressed, but the visitors could not recover from their defensive errors and missed chances. The result ended Everton’s three-match winless run. Everton left out Jack Grealish for a disciplinary breach; the Press Association reported that he had missed training without permission. Manager David Moyes backed the club’s decision but declined to discuss details. Everton next face Newcastle in the Premier League on Monday.

sports.content: The 6-0 Minnesota Vikings face the Detroit Lions on Sunday, Nov. 1, in an NFL Week 8 NFC North matchup. Minnesota is the league’s last unbeaten team; Detroit is 4-2. Baltimore also visits Buffalo, with Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson potentially returning. The week’s schedule ends Monday, Nov. 2, with Chicago at Seattle. The Bears-Seahawks game will feature two recent trade arrivals: Chicago acquired defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from Tennessee, and Seattle acquired guard Quenton Nelson from Indianapolis. Simmons is expected to make his Bears debut against the Seahawks. Four teams—Houston, New Orleans, the New York Giants and San Francisco—have a bye in Week 8.

sports.title: Carrick keeps Fernandes as captain ahead of United
sports.summary: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick says Bruno Fernandes will remain club captain after the pair held talks to resolve tension over the team’s tactics. sports.content: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick says Bruno Fernandes will remain club captain after the pair held talks to resolve tension over the team’s tactics. Carrick benched the midfielder for Sunday’s 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth after Fernandes questioned the approach in a 4-1 Champions League loss to Como. Carrick said the decision applied to that match and did not change Fernandes’ standing. United have gone eight matches without a win. Club leaders discussed Carrick’s position earlier this week but kept him in charge for Saturday’s Premier League visit to Chelsea. Carrick said he did not need assurances about his job and that Fernandes was committed to helping the team. Fernandes’ place in the starting lineup at Chelsea is still uncertain. United are seeking their first Premier League win since August 30.

sports.content: Sergio Garcia, the 2017 Masters champion, says he will leave LIV Golf and play on the DP World Tour in 2027, while keeping open the possibility of a return to the PGA Tour. The 46-year-old Spaniard also wants to qualify for Europe’s Ryder Cup team at Adare Manor in Ireland next September. He has played in the event 10 times and is its all-time leading points scorer, with 28.5. LIV is seeking to continue after Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund withdrew its support and the league filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection. New investor BC Partners Credit has pledged up to $300 million toward a proposed 2027 relaunch, but several prominent players have said they will not return. Garcia has also said he hopes to return to the Masters after apologizing for his conduct at Augusta in 2026. A return to the PGA Tour may have to wait until August 2027 under its 12-month suspension for LIV players.

sports.summary: Manchester United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo returned to partial team training on Wednesday and is in contention for Saturday’s Premier League visit to Chelsea, while striker Benjamin Sesko is expected to remain out until at least January with a recurring shin injury. sports.content: Manchester United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo returned to partial team training on Wednesday and is in contention for Saturday’s Premier League visit to Chelsea, while striker Benjamin Sesko is expected to remain out until at least January with a recurring shin injury. Manager Michael Carrick said the club is still assessing Sesko’s recovery as he heals. United are winless in eight matches across all competitions following a 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth. Sesko has scored twice this season, and his absence leaves United without an established centre-forward; Mainoo has missed the last four matches. United travel to Stamford Bridge on Saturday, October 31.
